The core insight is that NFL game events like touchdowns manifest as anomalous surges in tweet volume, which can be modeled as a convolution of a known temporal template with observed tweet rates. The matched filter approach leverages this by correlating the tweet-rate time series with a learned event signature, enabling real-time detection with low latency. Keyword filtering acts as a preprocessor to reduce noise and improve recall. Z-scoring normalizes tweet rates relative to baseline behavior, enhancing sensitivity to deviations. The system's robustness depends on accurate baseline estimation and learned temporal kernels. Failure modes include baseline drift, insufficient training data, or noisy keyword sets. The fusion of matched filters and keyword streams improves both true positive and false positive rates, as demonstrated in validation.
